assumptions: Cited, not re-derived, and NOT implemented.

STILL OPEN: that behavioural probing and parameter inspection exhaust the verification strategies available in this tree — an inference from the paper's taxonomy rather than a result in it (DEF-R7-VERIF-FAMILIES-EXHAUST).
STILL OPEN: the cited result is existential — it exhibits adversarial providers that defeat the surveyed strategies. It is not an impossibility theorem and this record does not claim one.
attrs.evidence: Cited, not re-derived. Zhang, Chen, Shen & Li (ICML 2024) construct two adversarial unlearning processes, one against each family of existing verification strategy, and show a dishonest provider passes verification while secretly retaining the data. Barez et al. (2025) record capability removal as open, with dual-use knowledge as the central obstacle. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ARTIFACT IS NARROW AND SHARP: GPT-5.6's EC-9 offers three dispositions for an affected descendant — reverify, quarantine, supersede. All three are dischargeable for an artifact you can delete and inspect. None is dischargeable for the WEIGHTS component of a support set, because the check that would confirm it is defeatable by the party being checked. So a revocation plan over an agent-world composite has a component on which it cannot close, and that is a property of the domain rather than of any implementation.

whoever controls the successor model in a replace-model operation

attrs.review_focus: SCOPED AT R7.1 ON GPT-5.6'S CORRECTION. R7's brief concluded that `a revocation plan over an agent-world composite has a component on which it cannot close`. That is too strong and only follows for the operation `KEEP this model and prove capability c was removed from its weights`. The architecture has another move: DISCARD M0, attach a fresh M1. For a post-training capability M1 never received, model replacement plus artifact revocation removes the capability without proving anything about unlearning — which is a benefit of treating the model as disposable, and is `replace-model` in mosaic/operations.json. The unlearning result binds the RETAIN-THE-MODEL branch only. For XOR neither branch works, and that is not an unlearning problem at all: f_XOR(∅)=1, so XOR is in the successor's independent capability basis and no replacement revokes it either. Read narrowly on purpose in the other direction too: the cited result is an EXISTENCE claim about adversarial providers under surveyed verification strategies, not an impossibility theorem.
attrs.statement: A capability's removal from model weights is not verifiable by the party that needs the guarantee: an adversarial provider can pass existing unlearning-verification strategies while retaining the information.
